title: Phase-stack doubling loop
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean-valued oracle on four indices and Boolean words, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $b$ be a Boolean value, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a register state. Suppose every register is at most $B$ and $T+2\,SP\leq B$. The machine reaches the move site that copies the phase stack back from phase $0$ of the doubling loop for $b$, with $SP=0$ and $T$ increased by twice its original $SP$; all other registers are unchanged and the result is unset. Every configuration before the final one satisfies the guard requiring valid instructions and registers at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ is a Boolean-valued oracle on four indices and Boolean words
every register of $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle on four indices and
Boolean words, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $b$ be a Boolean value, and let
$\mathrm{st}$ be a register state. If every register of $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$ and
$T+2\,SP\leq B$, the machine can run from the initial phase of the doubling loop to the
move site that copies the phase stack back, leaving $SP=0$ and replacing $T$ by its
original value plus twice its original $SP$, with all other registers unchanged and the
answer unset. Every configuration along the run satisfies the guard requiring valid
instructions and all registers at most $B$.
